Born at Windsor, Berkshire, about 1588, and educated at Eton and King's College,
Cambridge. He came to Massachusetts with John Winthrop's fleet in 1630 and was the first minister of the church in
Boston for the rest of his life. He was one of Anne Hutchinson's chief opponents in 1637,
and a hard enemy of the Quakers in the 1650s, the years when the Southwicks, also in this tree,
were driven out of Salem. He died at Boston on 7 August 1667.
Born at Henley-on-Thames in 1592, wife of the Reverend John Wilson.
She did not sail with him in 1630 and came over to Boston later.
Genealogists list her among the colonists with a royal descent, though that hasn't been checked here.
